newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait bourse index falls 90 points on loan curbs.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait bourse index falls 90 points on loan curbs.

text.p: Kuwait Stock Exchange's index dropped 90 points in the week to Wednesday mainly in response to the Central Bank's suspension of lending for equity trading, investors said on Thursday.
"The Central Bank's decision made some investors fear rapid selling at the start of the week when they thought the decision involved swift settlement of the debt," said an investor.
"The (Central Bank's) decision was the main reason for the fall," he added.

The Central Bank's curbs on lending for equity trading purposes were issued to banks on Thursday and were announced through the official news agency on Sunday after the end of the week's second trading session.
"It might take some weeks before the market overcomes the psychological impact of the Central Bank's decision," said another investor.

Loans for securities trading stand at 425 million dinars ($1.402 million) of which 96 million dinars were margin loans, the Central Bank said. The figure needs to be reduced by 130 million dinars by the end of 1997.
Some investors said they intrepreted the decision as a sign that the Central Bank expected a correction.
Economists have said the decision is meant to protect banks against any eventuality, noting that the market had overreacted to the decision.
The index finished the week at 2,349.3 points with losers leading gainers 47-9.

The daily average for value of traded shares fell to 61.7 million dinars from 76.6 million. Volume eased to a daily average of 223.3 million shares from 286 million, Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE) figures show.
Investment firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 98 million dinars, followed by property firms with 84 million and banks with 45.6 million.
United Industries, Investment Projects, United Realty, Pearl of Kuwait Real Estate and the Commercial Bank, were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
